To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the transcriptional coactivators CBP/p300 are required for the induction of IL-2 and IFN-g gene transcription in T cells and that this function is mediated through the recruitment of the coactivator to the promoter by the calcium-dependent transcription factor NFAT.

the calcium-dependent transcription factor, NFAT, is a critical regulator of gene expression after T cell activation, and that this regulation occurs through the action of the calcium-dependent transcription factors, NFAT and calcineurin, which are activated by calcium.
the TCR and CD3 complex, and the CD28 costimulatory receptor, regulate gene transcription through distinct mechanisms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of gene expression in T cells after activation.
the mechanisms of calcium signaling in T cells.
understanding how the immune system is regulated and how the immune system regulates the body's response to pathogens, cancer, and other insults.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the T cell receptor (TCR) is the most critical component in TCR signaling, and that the TCR complex is the most important component in TCR signal transduction.
the CRAC channel is the major calcium entry pathway in T lymphocytes and is essential for the activation of T cells.
the calcium signaling system is a key regulator in the activation of the TCR signaling pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CRAC channel, a key player in the regulation of Ca2+ entry into cells, is a highly regulated Ca2+ release-activated Ca2+ (CRAC) channel.
the CRAC channel is a calcium release activated calcium channel that is essential for T cell activation and that it is regulated in a number of different ways.
the CRAC channel is a critical component of the TCR signal transduction pathway, which is required for T cell proliferation and survival.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are a number of different mechanisms by which the calcium response can regulate transcription, and these mechanisms may not be mutually exclusive.
calcium is a critical regulator of gene expression after T cell activation and that this calcium dependent gene regulation occurs through the calcium dependent transcription factor NFAT (NFATc2).

the calcium signals are not only important for the transcriptional regulation of genes but also for the regulation of chromatin structure and chromatin remodeling, and this is a very important aspect of gene regulation.
